title: Alluvial Soil Characteristics & Farming Guide
characteristics: Formed by river silt deposition. Rich in Potash and Lime, but low in Nitrogen and Phosphoric Acid. High natural fertility and excellent workability.
water_retention: High to Moderate water holding capacity
content: Alluvial soil covers over 40% of India's land area, predominantly across the Indo-Gangetic plains and coastal deltas. It is the most productive agricultural soil. Supplement with Nitrogenous fertilizers (Urea) and Phosphatic fertilizers (DAP) for optimum yields.
source: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Soil Bureau

title: Black Soil (Regur Soil) Characteristics & Farming Guide
characteristics: Derived from basalt volcanic lava. High clay content (montmorillonite clay). Swells when wet and develops deep fissures/cracks when dry (self-ploughing property). High in Calcium, Potassium, Magnesium, and Carbonates.
water_retention: Very High (Retains moisture for extended drought periods)
content: Black soil is prominent across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Telangana. Its exceptional moisture retention capability makes it ideal for rainfed cotton, soybean, and Rabi chickpea crops. Requires careful irrigation management to prevent waterlogging during heavy monsoon downpours.
source: National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning (NBSS&LUP)

title: Red Soil Characteristics & Farming Guide
characteristics: Formed from crystalline igneous rocks. Red color due to high Iron Oxide (Fe2O3) content. Porous, friable structure. Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Humus, and Lime.
water_retention: Low to Moderate (Highly permeable, drains quickly)
fertility: Low to Medium (Responds very well to fertilizers & organic FYM)
content: Red soil covers vast areas of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and Chota Nagpur plateau. Due to low moisture retention, it is best suited for drought-tolerant rainfed crops, pulses, and oilseeds under sprinkler/drip irrigation.

title: Clay Soil Characteristics & Management
characteristics: Contains over 40% fine clay particles. Heavy texture, highly cohesive, forms sticky plastic mass when wet and hard clods when dry. High Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC).
water_retention: Very High (Slow drainage, prone to waterlogging)
content: Clay soils hold water and nutrients extremely well, making them perfect for puddled rice fields and sugarcane. Adding organic manure or gypsum improves soil structure and water infiltration.

title: Loamy Soil Characteristics & Farming Guide
characteristics: Ideal balanced mix of Sand (40%), Silt (40%), and Clay (20%). Soft, crumbly texture with optimal aeration, internal drainage, and organic humus content.
ph_range: 6.0 - 7.2 (Ideal neutral range for plant nutrient uptake)
content: Loam is considered the gold standard for agricultural cultivation. It offers easy root penetration, excellent microbial activity, and efficient fertilizer response across all crop species.

title: Sandy Soil Characteristics & Management
characteristics: Coarse texture with over 80% sand particles. High aeration, low nutrient retention, fast water infiltration, rapid warming in spring.
content: Sandy soils require frequent light irrigations and split applications of fertilizers to prevent nutrient leaching. Organic matter addition (FYM, compost) significantly improves water holding capacity.

title: Banana Suitable Soil & Land Preparation
content:
Well drained loamy soils are suitable for banana cultivation. Alkaline and saline soils should be avoided.
Season of planting
Wet lands
Garden lands
Hill Banana
Padugai lands
Poovan, Rasthali, Monthan, Karpooravalli and Neypoovan can be cultivated during February April. Nendran and Robusta can be cultivated during April May.
Banana can be cultivated in garden lands during January February and November December.
April May (lower Palani hills), June August (Sirumalai) are the suitable seasons for cultivating hill banana.
In Padugai lands, the crop can be cultivated during January February and August September.
Selection and pre-treatment of suckers
Select sword suckers of 1.5 to 2.0 kg weight which are free from diseases and nematodes. Trim the roots and decayed portion of the corm, cut the pseudostem leaving 20 cm from the corm and grade the suckers to size. To avoid wilt disease in Rasthali, Monthan, Virupakshi and other wilt susceptible varieties, infected portions of the corm may be pared and dipped for 5 minutes in 0.1% Emisan solution (1 g in 1 lit of water). Pralinage is done with 40 g of Carbofuran 3 G granules per sucker. (Dip the corm in slurry solution containing 4 parts clay plus 5 parts water and sprinkle Carbofuran to control nematodes). Alternatively,shade dry for atleast 24 hours and plant. Sow Sunhemp on 45th day; incorporate it after about a month.This operation reduces nematode build up. Use tissue cultured banana plants with 5-6 leaves. At the time of planting, apply 25 g Bacillus Subtils / plant.
Field preparation
Wet lands
No preparatory cultivation is necessary.
Garden land
2 4 ploughings are required before planting.
Padugai
One deep spade digging is essential.
Hill Banana
Clean the jungle and construct contour stone walls before planting. Digging Pits Wet lands

title: Mango Suitable Soil & Land Preparation
content:
Ideal soil for mango is red loamy. Good drainage is preferable for better establishment. Ideal pH range is from 6.5 to 8.0.
Season of planting
Planting spreads from July to December.
Planting material
Approach and epicotyl grafts are used for planting.

title: Sugarcane Suitable Soil & Land Preparation
content:
Performs well in all soil types and extremely well in garden land condition.  Good quality cane with higher yield.  Has multi ratooning capacity.  Can be grown throughout the year.  Gives higher recovery.  Self detrashing in nature.  Amenable for wide row spacing.
